passages.provision_quote: Any sentence enhancement that was imposed prior to January 1, 2018, pursuant to Section 11370.2 of the Health and Safety Code, except for any enhancement imposed for a prior conviction of violating or conspiring to violate Section 11380 of the Health and Safety Code is legally invalid.
passages.note: Bill retroactively voids certain sentencing enhancements and mandates resentencing to a lesser term unless public safety would be endangered.

rows.reasoning: SB 483 (2021-2022), authored by Allen and signed into law, retroactively invalidates specific prior sentencing enhancements and requires courts to resentence affected individuals to a lesser term unless a lesser sentence would endanger public safety. This shows a lean away from harsher punishment but its narrow, category-specific removal of enhancements does not match the operative clauses of any single rung on 'When someone breaks the law, how should the system respond?' (it does not establish a focus on support/treatment, a restitution framework, or a general case-by-case philosophy), so it separates direction but not the rungs on that side.
needs_source: Allen's own statements or floor remarks explaining the sentencing philosophy behind SB 483, or another chair-shaped record/statement on this topic
